items.abstract: Static credentials like Secure Shell (SSH) keys and personal access tokens (PATs) can create hidden security risks and headaches for teams. But there’s a better way. In this session, you’ll learn how to move beyond static credentials by using short-lived, ephemeral SSH certificates. We’ll show you how GitHub, combined with your identity provider and a certificate-issuing service, can eliminate the need for long-lived tokens — making access simpler, safer, and more scalable. You'll gain practical insights on how to improve your security posture, streamline credential management, and give developers a smoother, more secure experience.

You’ll leave with practical insights and next steps to help your organization start securing its cryptography today.

items.abstract:
Ever asked an AI coding agent to build something, only to get code that technically works but completely misses the mark? You’re not alone.

In this session, you’ll discover Spec Kit, an open source toolkit that changes how you collaborate with AI coding agents. Instead of tossing vague prompts into the void, you’ll learn how to create living specifications that guide AI to deliver exactly what you need.

We’ll show how Spec Kit turns chaotic “just build it” requests into clear, testable roadmaps. You’ll see how it breaks development into four validated phases, embeds your actual requirements, and adds checkpoints to catch issues before they become costly surprises.

Whether you’re using GitHub Copilot, Claude Code, or any other AI agent, you’ll leave knowing how to stay in the driver’s seat—steering, validating, and iterating with confidence instead of cleaning up after the fact.

participants.globalBio: Building GitHub Agentic Workflows

items.abstract:
AI agents are transforming software development. Today, you can assign tasks to agents in GitHub.com, in VS Code, and on the command line via Copilot CLI. But what if you didn’t have to assign tasks to your agents? What if they could do work on your behalf, continuously in the background, without you having to ask?

In GitHub Next, we’ve been exploring this idea, which we call “Continuous AI.” Just like continuous integration, Continuous AI is integrated into your development workflows and runs on GitHub Actions. But Continuous AI integrates LLMs and agents to do things that traditional continuous integration cannot – things that require judgement, that cannot be expressed as simple rules. They accelerate your team, not just individual developers.

In this talk, we will present the concept of Continuous AI, describe what kinds of tasks it is useful for, and show many examples of real Continuous AI workflows we are using in our own projects and with our collaborators in the open source community. We’ll show you how you can write your own Continuous AI workflows using our open-source tool, Agentic Workflows, as well as try out examples from the community.

This is a first look at experimental work from GitHub Next, GitHub's research and engineering team that focuses on shaping the future of software creation. If you’re curious about what’s coming next — and how to prepare for it — this session is for you.

That's why Docusign built 1FE (“One Frontend”), an open‑source micro frontend platform that enables autonomous teams to ship self‑contained widgets, while a shared runtime, governance layer, and GitHub‑native automation enforce consistency, security, and performance.

In this session, you'll discover how 1FE differs from classic module federation or forced monorepos; how teams hot‑reload local changes against live environments; and how centralized utilities (auth, feature flags, logging, design tokens) accelerate delivery. Expect architecture deep dives, a live workflow demo, real metrics (duplication, onboarding, release time), and a practical adoption playbook.
